newsitem.title: USA: Florida congressman to skip Senate race.
newsitem.headline: Florida congressman to skip Senate race.

text.p: Republican Congressman Bill McCollum of Florida said Monday he would not run for the Senate next year, ending speculation that he would take on the incumbent Democrat, Sen. Bob Graham.

"I would very much like the opportunity to serve the people of Florida in the United States Senate and expect to make a Senate race some day, but now is not the time," McCollum, 52, said in a statement. He said he had explored the possibility of a Senate race for several weeks before deciding against it.
Graham, 60, is a strong favourite to win re-election. He recently decided to seek a third Senate term rather than run again for governor, where he served for eight years.
Florida's other senator is Republican Connie Mack, 56, who is in his second term and will be up for re-election in 2000.
McCollum represents a central Florida district that includes part of Orlando. He is chairman of the House Crime subcommittee.
